27.0.s.en: (1) The daughters of Zelophehad and the laws of inheritance

27.0.0.en: When the people learned, after the census, that one of the purposes of this census was to divide the land among the clans of the tribes, five sisters (v. 33) came forward to Moses. They were the daughters of a man named Hepher, of the tribe of "Manasseh", and they had no brother to carry their father's name. They brought their complaint to Moses the leader of the people, to Eleazar the priest, and to the leaders and judges of the people, before the tabernacle of meeting.

27.1.0.en: The substance of the complaint was that their father had died and left them without brothers, so why should their father have no inheritance like the other men of his clan? In defense of their father they mentioned that he was not among the men of the rebellion of Korah and his company, who angered the Lord so that He destroyed them, but was an ordinary man who died like the rest of the people.

27.1.1.en: He died in his own sin: by this expression they meant that their father was like the rest of the people who died, either by the ancestral sin which all inherited from Adam .. or that he died like the others who murmured against entering the land, which was their sin, or that he was among those who died in the last plague, which took twenty-four thousand of the people.

27.2.0.en: This was a new matter for Moses, the man of God, so he did not make a decision on his own, but returned to God "before the Holy of Holies" to ask Him about this matter.

27.3.0.en: The Lord's answer to Moses came in favor of the five daughters. He commanded him that their father should have a portion like the rest of his brothers, and that they should inherit this portion from their father.

27.3.1.en: Here we learn two important things. The first is that Moses the servant returned to God when he met a matter that was new to him, and did not rely on himself or his own opinion in it ... May you too do likewise and return to God in all your affairs.

27.3.2.en: The second matter is the complaint of the daughters themselves. They came to the man of God to ask about their right to the land. May we learn from them this conduct, and go to the Church, according to the commandment of Christ, seeking guidance or arbitration when there is a dispute, instead of going to the courts or elsewhere.

27.4.0.en: God used this situation, the question of the daughters of Zelophehad, to establish some laws used in inheritance. They were as follows:

27.4.1.en: 1- If a man dies who has no sons, his inheritance passes in full to his daughter.

27.4.2.en: 2- If a man dies who has no offspring at all, his brothers inherit his land and possessions.

27.4.3.en: 3- If there are no brothers or sons, the land returns to the paternal uncles and is distributed among them.

27.4.4.en: 4- If there is none of the above, the land and the inheritance are distributed among his kinsmen (his cousins) who bear the name of the man's grandfather.

27.4.5.en: These laws were observed by all the people of Israel all the days of their lives.

27.5.s.en: (2) The death of Moses and Joshua's succession

27.5.0.en: Mount Abarim: a range of mountains east of the Jordan. The word Abarim means "beyond the Jordan" or opposite the river, and these are the mountains on which Balaam and Balak king of Moab went up (chs. 23, 24) (Map 6). In this verse God calls Moses to go up to the top of a mountain or high hill, one of the hills of the mountain lying east of the river Jordan, and asks him to look well at the land that God had promised His people. We also learn that the name of this hill was "Nebo", which is the summit of the headland of Pisgah, lying north of the Dead Sea. It is noticed that God said to Moses, "Behold the land which I have given", although He had not yet given it; but since God has promised, His word is sure, and the people are considered to have already possessed it.

27.6.0.en: Although God had punished Moses by not allowing him to enter the land (v. 14), yet in His tenderness He is gentle toward him and makes him go up and look at the land, the inheritance of his people, so that his soul rejoices in the work of God and His fulfillment of His promises. God also tells him that this would be the last thing he would do in his life before his departure and death.

27.7.0.en: God reminds Moses of the reason for the punishment and for his not entering the land. These are the events recounted in detail in (ch. 20). In summary, the people murmured because of the lack of water, and God commanded him to speak to the rock, but when he fell into anger he struck the rock, and even rebuked the people. God considered this a sin of disobedience, and its punishment was that Moses would not enter the land.

27.8.0.en: Moses asked nothing for himself, but accepted what the Lord announced to him in submission and surrender, and was content to see the land from every side (Deut 3:27). But with the heart of a father who is not concerned for his own life so much as for the future of his children, he asked God, the Creator of all mankind, to choose a man after him to take over the leadership of all the people.

27.9.0.en: The task of this new leader would be to lead and guide the multitudes of this people: to bring them out of their present place, bring them into the new land, and divide it among the tribes and clans. These words show Moses' concern for his people to the last moments of his life, for he did not want the people to be scattered like a flock of sheep that has no shepherd.

27.10.0.en: In whom is the Spirit: that is, a man who has heart, zeal and fervor.

27.10.1.en: God chose "Joshua", the closest disciple of Moses, and the Lord states the reason for choosing him, namely that he possessed the spirit of leadership and love for the people. He commands Moses to lay his hand on him, as a clear sign before the people that "Joshua" was taking over the leadership.

27.10.2.en: Note: the laying on of hands is an ancient custom that was known among the nations. Jacob laid his hands on "Ephraim and Manasseh" for blessing. The laying on of hands here means:

27.10.3.en: 1- The appointment and installation of Joshua before the people.

27.10.4.en: 2- A sign to the people that the days of Moses were drawing to a close, so that they might prepare themselves psychologically for it.

27.10.5.en: 3- The expression of the laying on of hands was taken up by the Church in her New Covenant as a sign of the giving of the Holy Spirit to the faithful through the pure Apostles, and after them the Fathers the bishops (Acts 19:6), and it also came about through the anointing with the Holy Myron for the Fathers the priests.

27.10.6.en: 4- The expression of the laying on of hands is also used of the one who receives the sacrament of the priesthood in the holy Church of God, for the bishop lays his hand on the head of the candidate and declares his ordination and his rank as well, whether a consecrated deacon or a priest.

27.10.7.en: God chose Joshua to lead the people because of his distinction in many spiritual situations, which are:

27.10.8.en: 1- He was the servant of Moses, clinging to him, and he was discipled at his hands. When Moses spoke with God in a tent outside the camp of Israel and the glory of God appeared to him, and then left the tent, Joshua remained standing before the tent until Moses returned (Ex 33:11).

27.10.9.en: 2- He led the people in their war with Amalek and defeated them, the first war that the children of Israel faced after their exodus from Egypt (Ex 17).

27.10.10.en: 3- He was the only one who accompanied Moses when he went up the mountain, and he continued waiting for him on the mountain forty days until he received the commandments and the Law and the design of the tabernacle of meeting.

27.10.11.en: 4- He spied out the Promised Land with his companions, and returned with Caleb glorifying God and encouraging the people to enter the Promised Land, despite the murmuring of the ten fellow spies, which made the people rebel against God (ch. 14).

27.11.0.en: To complete the choice and installation of Joshua, God also asks Moses to take Joshua before all the people and before Eleazar the priest and to charge him in their presence, so that the priest and the people would be the witnesses. Moses also surrounds him with awe and respect and commands the people to obey and submit to the new leader, so that Joshua would have the place of Moses in the hearts of the people.

27.12.0.en: The Urim: the Urim and Thummim were two stones that the high priest placed on his breast. Through these two stones the answer of the Lord came to the questions and requests of the people, by their shining or not, so that the high priest knew the mind of God, whether it was affirmative or negative.

27.12.1.en: Although Joshua was the leader of his people, God commands him not to bring anything from himself, but just as Moses used to return to God in every matter, so Joshua must also return in every matter to the high priest (Eleazar or his successor), so that God's mind in everything might be made clear. The means by which God made known His will was the two stones, the Urim and Thummim. Consequently Joshua himself would be subject to all the divine commands.

27.13.0.en: As God spoke, Moses did exactly what God had commanded him in the preceding verses, and Joshua was installed as the successor of Moses by the laying on of hands and by his acceptance of all the commandments.

27.13.1.en: It is noticed that Moses had sons, but he did not think of appointing one of them as leader over the people. Instead he appointed the one whom God chose, who was the best spiritually and personally.

27.13.2.en: In the last moments of Moses' life, and in his last conversation with God, Moses thought of nothing but a successor for his people, for the good of this people ...

27.13.3.en: So if you are a person in charge, or a leader, or even a father at the level of your family, take care to teach leadership to others and involve others with you, so that the work may continue and the good may continue. Many people's projects ended with the end of their lives because they did not care to involve others and took the front in everything themselves.

28.0.s.en: (1) The daily offerings and burnt offerings

28.0.0.en: God first commanded Moses concerning the presentation of offerings at the beginning of the second year after their exodus from Egypt (Ex 40:2), (Lev 1..). Before their entry into the new land He reminds them once again, especially since the first generation that came out of Egypt had all perished.

28.1.0.en: My offering: that is, the sacrifices and gifts with which a person draws near to God.

28.1.1.en: My bread: a figurative expression meaning that what a person offers to God is considered a feast to honor Him. And made by fire: that is, what was kindled and burned on the altar.

28.1.2.en: A sweet savor: that is, God was pleased with them and accepted them with satisfaction and love from His children.

28.1.3.en: God's commandment to Moses was that the people should not neglect the divine offerings which He had already mentioned many times. The expression "in their due season" means care and watchfulness for the honor of God, for nothing that concerns God should be postponed, because this postponement is a kind of slackness in respecting the name of the holy God.

28.1.4.en: My beloved brother, these words apply even more to us. You must not delay your tithes, your vows or your offerings, for it is not right to neglect God in His rights, when He is the giver of all good things.

28.2.0.en: In the following verses (3-8) is an explanation of the offering of the continual burnt offering, whose provisions included the following:

28.2.1.en: 1- A lamb in the morning, one year old (a yearling), without blemish or disease, burned completely on the altar of burnt offering every morning.

28.2.2.en: 2- Another exactly like it, which was offered in the evening. The expression "between the two evenings" means after the afternoon (the first evening) and at the end of the sunset (the second evening).

28.3.1.en: 3- There was also offered with each sacrifice separately fine flour mingled with pure olive oil beaten out, that is, the fruit was beaten so that the oil flowed from it. As for the quantities, they were about (2.29) liters for the flour, with half a liter of oil, by present measures and volumes.

28.3.2.en: This offering, that is, the burnt offering, was daily and continual. God reminds them that they had offered it in Sinai, so they must offer it also in the land of Canaan and not make light of it after their rest in the new land.

28.4.0.en: Strong wine: that is, good, aged wine.

28.4.1.en: A drink offering of good wine, in the amount of half a liter, was also offered with each lamb and the flour mingled with oil (see ch. 15:5).

28.5.0.en: God again emphasizes to Moses that just as he did in the morning offering, he must repeat all of it, with the same offerings, with the evening sacrifice, which was offered between the afternoon and sunset.

28.6.s.en: (2) The offerings and burnt offerings of the Sabbath day

28.6.0.en: Because of the importance of the Sabbath day and its standing, and its being considered the most important day of worship in the week, the offering is doubled. A lamb is offered in the morning and another in the evening, besides the daily offering, and all this also includes the flour and the poured wine, as a type and in the same amount as is offered in the daily sacrifice.

28.6.1.en: Note: the morning and evening sacrifices, as well as the additional Sabbath sacrifices, are burnt offerings offered entirely to God, and the priest eats nothing of them. As for the offerings of flour mingled with oil, the priest would take from them a handful and burn it on the altar, while the rest of it the priests would take as their portion.

28.6.2.en: May the Lord's day be honored in your eyes, so that you offer in it more worship than usual, and love and service to others, remembering that your life was renewed on this day by the Resurrection of Christ, so that you care for spiritual things more than material things.

28.7.s.en: (3) The offerings of the beginnings of the months

28.7.0.en: The Jewish year was a lunar year, and the month began with the observation of the appearance of the crescent moon. The first day of the month was a spiritual as well as a social celebration. God commanded Moses that there should be a special offering for the beginnings of the months, and this offering consisted of:

28.7.1.en: 1- Two bulls 2- A mature male sheep (a ram) 3- Seven lambs one year old. God commanded the keeping of a feast at the beginnings of the months for the following reasons:

28.7.2.en: 1- That they might know that God is the Creator of the universe and the ruler of time, so that in every period of time, which is a month, they offer Him worship.

28.7.3.en: 2- The pagans used to offer acts of worship at the beginnings of the months, so God wanted to occupy them with His worship rather than with idols, and gave them the keeping of a feast at the beginnings of the months in place of the customs of the pagans.

28.8.0.en: As usual, these sacrifices or burnt offerings were not offered alone, but the flour mingled with oil and the drink offering of wine had to be offered with them. It is to be observed that the quantities and measures which God set with each offering were proportionate to the size of the animal slaughtered, whether more or less, and this was already discussed in (ch. 15). The meaning we draw from all this is that God does not want us to forget Him in our celebrations, our feasts and our joys, for He alone is the source of our delight and joy, and we must not be preoccupied with material joys and with eating and drinking, but make God a partner with us in everything, so that we taste the meaning of the true joy that God gives to His children.

28.9.0.en: The burnt offerings that were offered at the feasts of the beginnings of the months were also accompanied by the offering of a male goat as a sin offering, so that God might take away the sins of His people. God reminds Moses and his people that all these offerings particular to the beginning of the month do not cancel the morning and evening burnt offering, nor do they take its place, but are additions to it.

28.9.1.en: It is good that you remember God on all occasions, not only every year but every month, every week and every day, so that you sit and account for your sins, and think of God's kindnesses to you, to thank Him and to contemplate His love.

28.10.s.en: (4) The feast of the Passover and of Unleavened Bread

28.10.0.en: Because of the utmost importance of the feast of the Passover, and the remembrance of God's work of redemption in the salvation of the people of the children of Israel and their exodus from the land of Egypt and the redemption of their firstborn by the blood of the Passover lamb, God reviews with His people what He had said to them before in (Ex 12), (Lev 23) and also (Deut 16), about the duty of celebrating the feast of the Passover at its usual time, which is the fourteenth day of the month of Abib (Nisan) every year; and this was a type of what Christ did for us.

28.10.1.en: After the eating of the Passover, beginning from the fifteenth day of the month and for 7 days, nothing is eaten but unleavened bread, that is, bread without leaven. The feast of Unleavened Bread is from the fifteenth day to the twenty-first day of the month of Abib, in addition to the eating of unleavened bread at the feast of the Passover, which is the fourteenth day.

28.11.0.en: It is stated in this verse, as it will also be stated in (v. 25), that both the first day and the seventh day of Unleavened Bread are considered holy convocations to the Lord, so that on them a person may not do any work, exactly like the law of the Sabbath day. This emphasis from God is so that His people might reflect and remember the spiritual meanings in the feasts and occasions, that they are works of salvation, and we should not be too busy to remember them and reflect on them.

28.12.0.en: These verses include an explanation of the offerings that were offered every day throughout the seven days, from the day after the feast of the Passover for seven days. Their details were as follows:

28.12.1.en: 1- Daily burnt offerings of two bulls, one ram and seven lambs one year old, and all these are offered with the flour mingled with oil and the drink offering of wine in the proportions explained previously.

28.12.2.en: 2- A he-goat, that is, a male goat, is also offered as a sin offering to make atonement for the sins of the people. God reminds His people that all these offerings are offered every day throughout the week of Unleavened Bread, and this is in addition to the daily offering, that is, the morning burnt offering and the evening burnt offering.

28.13.0.en: A confirmation of what is stated in (v. 18), that the seventh day is like the first day of Unleavened Bread, so that the two days are considered feasts on which no work is done.

28.13.1.en: My beloved brother, God cared greatly about public worship, so much that He repeated it again and again to emphasize it!! ... If this was so in the days of animal sacrifices, how much more with the sacrifice of His only Son our Lord Jesus Christ ... Take care, beloved, about the prayer of the Liturgy, and do not be slack or postpone attending it, for it is a holy convocation to the Lord which God made for your salvation and deliverance. Do you truly understand and feel this?!

28.14.0.en: The discussion of this feast came in more detail in (Lev 23:15-21). The day of the firstfruits: the feast of harvest or the feast of Pentecost (the fiftieth day), on which the firstfruits of the produce were offered to God on the occasion of the wheat harvest. This is distinct from the first feast of firstfruits on the first Sunday after the Passover (in the view of the Sadducees), which was called the feast of the wave offering (Lev 23:9-14). When you bring a new meat offering to the Lord in your weeks: the day of firstfruits came 7 weeks after the feast of the waving of the barley before the Lord, "that is, the first feast of firstfruits", and therefore what is meant is the feast of harvest and not the feast of firstfruits which comes on the first Sunday after the feast of the Passover. At the feast of Pentecost a person offered the firstfruits of his land of wheat to God in the form of two loaves of new wheat with their appointed sacrifices (Lev 23:17). And God commanded His people to do no work in their celebration of this day, like the rest of the holy convocations of the Lord.

28.15.0.en: A repetition of what God had already explained in the preceding verses of the same chapter: the offering of two bulls and a ram as burnt offerings and a goat as a sin offering, with all their offerings of flour and the drink offering, and all this besides the daily burnt offerings represented by the morning sacrifice and the evening sacrifice as well. They shall be unto you without blemish: that is, all the sacrifices offered to God are to be free from defects.

28.15.1.en: How beautiful it is to offer the firstfruits to God, so that you feel His blessing in everything you have, and God becomes a partner in your life, so that you are at ease and rejoice. And know that His blessing is far greater than your gifts, but keep Him always before you, with His hand stretched out, so that He takes before you take, and your whole life is for Him.

28.15.2.en: The feasts of the seventh month, an introduction: the Jews had two calendars, one civil and the other religious, and both had the same names for the months of the year!! How was this?

28.15.3.en: When the people kept the Passover for the first time in Egypt, it was in the seventh month of the ordinary Jewish year. Because of the importance of this feast and this occasion, God commanded that this month also (with the same name) be the head and first of the months of the new religious calendar, and consequently the eighth month in the civil calendar (with the same name) became the second month in the Jewish religious year ... And this chapter speaks of the seventh month in the Jewish religious calendar, which therefore corresponds to the first month of the civil year, the month of "Tishrin the First", or its Hebrew name "Ethanim".
